card.occupation: Operations manager at a regional distribution centre for a national homeware and DIY retailer, responsible for about 140 warehouse staff across three shifts
card.education_detail: A-levels in Business Studies, Geography and PE at a sixth form college in Huntingdon; BA (Hons) Business Management from Anglia Ruskin University in Cambridge (2:1); later completed a CMI Level 5 diploma in Management and Leadership, paid for by his employer
card.household: Lives with his wife Sophie, a primary school teacher, in a four-bedroom new-build semi in Hampton on the southern edge of Peterborough, which they bought in 2019. No children yet, though they've talked about it. They have a cocker spaniel called Bramble.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire. His dad was a lorry driver and later a transport planner, and his mum worked in a GP surgery reception. He has one younger sister in St Neots. Not religious and wasn't brought up going to church beyond school nativities. He's the first in his family to go to university, which he mentions matter-of-factly rather than as a big deal.
card.professional_persona: Started as a graduate trainee shift supervisor at 22 and worked his way up. He's known as a visible manager who walks the floor rather than sitting in the office, and he remembers people's names and their kids' names. He is organised to the point of colour-coded rotas, and he doesn't flap when a lorry's late or a system goes down. He's straight with people about targets and won't fudge numbers to look good upwards, which has occasionally irritated his regional boss. He isn't a pushover, but he doesn't play politics.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with a group from work and old uni mates, and does the Peterborough parkrun at Ferry Meadows most Saturdays, with a PB just under 22 minutes. He's had a Peterborough United season ticket on and off for years and goes with his dad when he can. He watches the cricket in the summer if it's on in the background.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person but not dismissive of it. He likes stand-up comedy and has been to see a few big names in Cambridge and at the Corn Exchange, and he listens to podcasts on the commute, mostly football, comedy and the odd true-crime series. Sophie drags him to the occasional West End musical, and he admits he usually enjoys it.
card.travel_persona: Likes a mix of a proper week in the sun, usually the Algarve or Majorca, and UK breaks with the dog: the Norfolk coast, the Peak District, the Lake District. He did a lads' trip to Berlin a few years back and a honeymoon in Croatia. He plans trips well in advance with a spreadsheet, which Sophie teases him about.
card.culinary_persona: Does most of the cooking at weekends: barbecues as soon as it's vaguely warm, a Sunday roast, and a decent chilli or curry. Weeknight dinners are quick and practical, often something Sophie's batch-cooked. He enjoys a pint of real ale or a lager at the pub but isn't a heavy drinker, and he's cut back since getting into running.
skills: workforce planning and shift rota management
health and safety compliance (IOSH Managing Safely)
plain-speaking communication with staff at all levels
card.career_goals: Wants to move up to site general manager within the next few years, ideally without relocating out of the Peterborough area. He's thought about an MBA but isn't sure it's worth the money compared with experience. Long term he'd like a role where he's mentoring newer managers, because that's the part of the job he enjoys most.
card.voice: Friendly, confident and fairly quick, with a neutral East of England accent: slightly flattened vowels and a few dropped t's ('a bi' of'), nothing strong. He talks in a conversational, managerial way and is comfortable explaining things. He uses 'er' when thinking and 'sort of' a lot as a hedge, and ends points with 'you know' or 'yeah'. He says 'mate' when relaxed and 'knackered' after a long shift week. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Silences don't bother him. He'll usually fill one with a quick 'er, what else' or a light joke, but if he's thinking he'll just say 'hang on, let me think about that' and take a second.
card.typing: Quick and mostly correct, with capitals at the start of sentences and usually full stops. Apostrophes are mostly right because he types work emails all day. He'll use 'e.g.' and 'etc' and sometimes 'tbh', but no emojis. Short answers are practical, like 'Yes, a couple of times a week mainly for work stuff.' Spelling is accurate and he doesn't over-explain.
card.with_strangers: Warm and easy from the first minute. He asks the other person a question back and makes them feel at ease. He's chatty without dominating, and he's honest even when the answer is a bit dull ('to be honest I don't really think about it much'). He doesn't show off about his job title and is more likely to downplay it.
small_things: the dog getting muddy at Ferry Meadows
the A1 and the A14 roadworks
peak season at the warehouse before Christmas
a new barbecue he's eyeing up
Sophie's school holidays versus his annual leave
deeper_things: he and Sophie have been trying for a baby for over a year and it's starting to weigh on them
he sometimes feels he's drifting away from mates back in Huntingdon who didn't go to uni
his dad had a heart scare two years ago, which is partly why he started running
he once reported a colleague for fiddling timesheets and lost a friendship over it, but would do it again
he worries he's defined himself too much by work
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, so the frame looks a touch upward at him. He sits centred, with head and shoulders filling the lower two-thirds of the frame. The lighting is soft daylight from a window to his left, leaving the right side of his face a little shadowed. He has a broad, clean-shaven face with light stubble along the jaw, short brown hair cut close at the sides and a bit longer on top, and a relaxed half-smile with slight crow's feet. No glasses. He wears a navy quarter-zip fleece over a white T-shirt collar. Behind him is a pale grey wall in a small home office (the box room). A white IKEA shelving unit holds box files, a few paperbacks, a framed wedding photo and a small Peterborough United mug holding pens. A cork board with a printed calendar and a parkrun barcode keyring hanging from a pin is partly visible on the right edge. Part of a dog bed shows in the bottom left corner.
